title: Why Can an F1 Pit Stop Take Only 2 Seconds?
description:
In less time than it takes you to read this sentence, a Formula One team can lift a car, change all four tyres and send it back into the race. The record is one point eight seconds. That is not luck. Every tool in the pit box was designed for that number, from a gun that spins a nut in a blink to the lights that tell the driver to go. Today, ten parts of the F1 pit stop, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:13 1. The wheel gun
2:30 2. The single wheel nut
3:45 3. The front jack
4:59 4. The tyre blankets
6:21 5. The coloured stripes
7:41 6. The pit lane speed limiter
9:04 7. The release lights
10:19 8. The missing fuel hose
11:38 9. The pit crew
12:54 10. The pit board
13:55 The verdict

Sources:
- Pit stop procedure and crew roles: Wikipedia, "Pit stop" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pit_stop
- Fastest pit stop, McLaren 1.80 s, 2023 Qatar Grand Prix: Formula1.com https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/mclaren-break-world-record-for-fastest-pit-stop-in-f1-history.html
- Wheel tethers and wheel retention: Wikipedia, "Formula One car" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_car
- Tyre compounds, colours and the two-compound rule: Wikipedia, "Formula One tyres" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_tyres
- Tyre blanket temperature limits: Wikipedia, "Formula One tyres" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_tyres
- Refuelling (1994-2009, banned 2010) and Verstappen fire, 1994 German Grand Prix: Wikipedia, "Refuelling in Formula One" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refuelling_in_Formula_One
- Massa fuel hose, 2008 Singapore Grand Prix: Wikipedia, "2008 Singapore Grand Prix" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Singapore_Grand_Prix
- Pit lane speed limit: FIA Formula One Sporting Regulations https://www.fia.com/regulation/category/110
